subject: Geography
description: Sahara, Gobi, Atacama, Thar — hot and cold deserts

questions.stem: The largest hot desert in the world is the:
questions.explanation: The Sahara — about 9 million km² — is the largest hot desert in the world, stretching across 10+ North African countries. If 'largest desert overall' is meant, Antarctica is larger (it is classified as a cold desert, ~14 million km²). The Gobi (cold desert — Mongolia and China) is about 1.3 million km²; Kalahari (southern Africa) ~0.9 million km²; Arabian ~2.3 million km².
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Thar desert, also known as the Great Indian Desert, lies chiefly in:
questions.explanation: The Thar desert covers ~200,000 km² across western Rajasthan (largest share), Gujarat (Kachchh), Punjab and Haryana, and extends into Pakistan's Sindh and Cholistan. Rajasthan accounts for ~60 %. The Indira Gandhi Canal (completed in stages since 1986) has brought canal irrigation to parts of the desert, making some crop farming possible.

questions.stem: The Atacama desert, often called the driest (non-polar) place on Earth, lies in:
questions.explanation: The Atacama lies in northern Chile and is the driest non-polar desert — some weather stations have recorded essentially no rainfall for decades. Cold Humboldt current offshore + rain shadow of the Andes create the aridity. It is a major site for astronomical observatories (ALMA, VLT, Cerro Tololo) because of the clear dark skies, and produces most of the world's lithium (for EV batteries) and copper.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Gobi desert, a cold desert of Central Asia, lies mainly in:
questions.explanation: The Gobi — 'waterless place' in Mongolian — covers southern Mongolia and the Inner Mongolia region of northern China. It is a cold desert — summers are hot, winters freezing, and snow is possible. Not a sand desert mostly — largely rocky / gravelly terrain. Dinosaur fossils at the Flaming Cliffs (including the first Velociraptor) are from the Gobi.

questions.stem: Match the desert with its continent. A. Patagonian. B. Kalahari. C. Great Victoria. D. Mojave. List-II: 1. South America, 2. Africa, 3. Australia, 4. North America.
questions.explanation: Patagonian — Argentina (South America), cold semi-arid. Kalahari — Botswana, Namibia, South Africa. Great Victoria — largest desert of Australia. Mojave — south-western USA (Death Valley is in the Mojave). Other world deserts worth knowing — Sonoran (USA/Mexico), Karakum (Turkmenistan), Namib (Namibia — oldest desert in the world).

questions.stem: Antarctica is technically classified as a:
questions.explanation: Antarctica receives less than 200 mm of precipitation a year on average (most as snow), which qualifies it as a desert. It is by that measure the largest desert on Earth (~14 million km²). Very low humidity and extreme cold mean plant life is essentially limited to mosses and lichens near the coast. The interior is among the driest places on the planet.

questions.stem: The term 'wadi', often used in discussions of desert landforms, refers to a:
questions.explanation: A wadi (Arabic) is a valley or dry stream bed that carries water only during rare rainstorms. Flash floods in wadis are a serious hazard in Middle-Eastern / North African deserts. Sand dunes — ergs (big sand seas), barchans (crescent-shaped dunes); an oasis — green patch with natural water; salt pans (sabkhas) are flat evaporite surfaces, e.g., Rann of Kachchh.
